effect: Ciprofloxacin may increase the anticoagulant effect of oral anticoagulants including warfarin.
mechanism: The label says the contribution of ciprofloxacin to increased INR is difficult to assess and can vary with infection age and general status.
guidance: The cited label recommends frequent prothrombin time and INR monitoring during and shortly after co-administration. Medication changes require a prescriber or anticoagulation clinician.
limitation: Applies to co-administration with an oral anticoagulant; this tool cannot estimate an individual INR or bleeding risk.

effect: Tetracyclines may increase anticoagulant effect in patients receiving anticoagulant therapy.
mechanism: The doxycycline label states that tetracyclines can depress plasma prothrombin activity.
guidance: The cited label notes that anticoagulant dosage may require clinician adjustment. Do not change either medicine without the treating clinician.
limitation: The label describes the tetracycline class and does not quantify an individual effect size or timing window.

effect: Thyroid hormone can increase the anticoagulant activity of oral anticoagulants.
mechanism: The label describes increased catabolism of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors with impaired compensatory clotting-factor synthesis.
guidance: The cited label recommends careful prothrombin time monitoring and clinician-directed anticoagulant adjustment.
limitation: Applies to oral anticoagulants; effect depends on thyroid status and therapy changes and is not a same-dose timing rule.

effect: Chronic oral acetaminophen at 4000 mg per day has increased INR in some warfarin-treated patients.
mechanism: The label reports an observed INR increase but does not establish the effect of short-term use.
guidance: The cited label says more frequent INR assessment may be appropriate. This rule is not a dose recommendation and does not generalize the chronic high-dose finding to occasional use.
limitation: The evidence is specifically chronic oral acetaminophen at 4000 mg per day; this event model does not capture dose or duration.

effect: Warfarin and NSAIDs including ibuprofen have synergistic effects on gastrointestinal bleeding risk.
mechanism: Warfarin impairs coagulation while NSAIDs affect platelet function and gastrointestinal mucosa.
guidance: The cited label advises caution with concomitant use. This tool cannot estimate an individual's bleeding risk.
limitation: The label describes a class interaction and does not provide a universal timing interval that removes the risk.

effect: Aspirin is listed among antiplatelet agents that can increase bleeding risk with warfarin.
mechanism: Antiplatelet activity can add to warfarin-associated impairment of coagulation.
guidance: The cited warfarin label recommends close monitoring when medicines that increase bleeding risk are started or stopped.
limitation: Indication dose and patient factors affect clinical decisions; this is not a same-dose timing rule.

effect: Increased INR and prothrombin time have been reported with concomitant PPI and warfarin use.
mechanism: The interaction may increase anticoagulant effect in some patients.
guidance: The cited label recommends monitoring INR and prothrombin time and adjusting warfarin only under clinical supervision.
limitation: The label does not provide an effect size or a timing interval that removes the interaction.

effect: Postmarketing reports suggest azithromycin may potentiate oral anticoagulants including warfarin.
mechanism: A dedicated study did not change prothrombin time but postmarketing reports describe possible potentiation.
guidance: The cited label recommends careful prothrombin-time monitoring during concomitant use.
limitation: The evidence includes postmarketing reports and a negative dedicated interaction study; individual effect size is unknown.
